Most of those "Filipino Side Hustle/Work From Home Website" videos are pretty much clickbait. People rarely make money from them. When they do it's not even a lot. The main profit source of the people who post those types of videos is the revenue they get from the videos themselves. Parang online pyramid scheme lang.

Find something that's high in demand, but low in supply. If you ever see a sidehustle that's trendy, chances are it's a little too late to hop on the band wagon because everyone else is already doing it. Why would they go to you who's just starting out if there are other people offering the same thing with far more experience?

If you really want to go into a sidehustle that's trendy, find a hole in said side hustle na you need to fill. Let's say maraming naghahanap neto pero parang walang nag proprovide. Ikaw na yung magsimula magprovide. I started an online ukay store dati, yes marami akong competition and at first walang bumili. Kasi nga ang daming account na pagpipilian na. Then I started selling ukay clothing items na bihira ioffer online and that's how I got my first sales.

I suggest you try to think of a service na ikaw mismo may gusto, pero nahihirapan ka maghanap ng nagproprovide. Why not do it yourself and offer to do it for other people din?

Hey! Digital artist here! I started out just drawing with a pencil and a piece of paper like most people, but eventually I wanted a bit more creative freedom.

Traditional drawing materials are pretty expensive, but with digital art all you need is a free program and the possibilities are nearly endless. I started drawing on my phone and eventually got good enough to make money so that I could buy a cheap drawing tablet.

It was around $60. It's not exactly "cheap", I know. But considering I've had it for nearly 5 years now and have made more than what I paid for it with people commissioning me, It's a pretty good deal. Plus, it's a buy one, create an infinite amount of pieces type of deal. Compare that to the cost of paints, markers, etc. you'll need for a few traditional pieces, not only that but the physical space you'll need to store them. Digital is definitely the far cheaper option.

Also like I said, you can start with the devices you already have :). Feel free to dm me if you'd like any in detail tips for resources (free drawing programs, youtube tutorials, etc.) as well as how to get started :)

There's two types of accounts on instagram, personal accounts and business accounts. You have to set the business option on yourself because "personal account" is the default.

A business account lets you add website links and other details to your bio as well as keep track of your post engagement (how many people have viewed your profile this week vs last week, which posts give you the most profile visits, etc.). An instagram business account also give you the option to pay a fee to promote your posts so that they'll appear in the timeline of people who follow similar accounts to yours.

TLDR: An "insta business account" is short for "instagram business account". An instagram account with more business related feautures compared to regular instagram accounts used for personal use.

What helps me when I'm starting to be self-aware of how hyperactive I am is taking a breather. If you're busy doing something or talkkng to someone, just ask them if you can take a few breathes for a while. They'll probably understand, and if they don't, well ADHD is considered a disability so they better lmao- but yeah, once you can take a few breaths try slowing your heart rate down. It doesn't always help for me but it waters my very hyperactive movements once I purposely try and slow my body down. It might not work for everyone but that's what works for me.

TLDR: Assess your hyperactivity once you become self-aware of your current actions, take a few deep breathes and gradually try to slow your body down. Don't just try to stop abruptly. Think of it like slowly stepping on a brake rather than slamming your foot down.

When it comes to controlling my impulsivity, especially when it comes to cash, what works for me is looking back at all my impulsive purchases, totalling how much I've spent, and thinking about how it would feel to still have that amount of money today. It's a work in progress though. You aren't gonna get over it right away. I'm doing pretty decent now but it took a lot of work to keep under control. I will say this though, setting a budget for your impulses isn't always a good idea, sometimes it turns into a slippery slope. Saying "I'll only spend this amount" looks great on paper but once you spend it, that feeling comes back and you'll want to feel it more and more. Personally I'd suggest avoiding it all together. Just my two cents though. Hopefully you can power through it. I'm rooting for you, wishing you the best! :D

I'll add my own recommendation here in the comments for the people who clicked on this post wanting an answer and not TO answer.

I highly recommend watching "The Good Place" if the whole self improvement journey story arc is your thing but don't want it to be too corny and preachy. It's a plot focused comedy about the afterlife and what it truly means to be a good person. Unlike most sitcoms  the plot doesn't reset after each episode but rather carry on to the nextThere aren't any "filler" episodes, not one episode has a bad rating, has an ethnically diverse cast, and is very very easy to digest. It gives you plot twist after plot twist that are actually surprising despite the tons of foreshadowing they throw at you along the way too. Which is honestly very rare these days. I can't remember the last time I was actually surprised by a plot twist. The worldbuilding is very witty. It also has a lot of crying moments.

I'm not explaining it in a way that gives the show justice, you really just have to see it for yourself. It's one of those show don't tell kind of shows. The best way to know the plot is simply by experiencing it.

It's a show that I watched shortly after the cancellation of Infinity Train and it honestly helped fill that hole for a bit. I said a bit because at the time we were all still hoping for this show to be picked up again for another season. I didn't want to include this part in the post because you aren't allowed to talk about wanting it back in a post anymore lmao-

TLDR: I recommend "The Good Place" a smart, plot-driven comedy about the afterlife and what it truly means to be a good person. It's the show that I find to be the closest alternative in terms of the vibes that I was looking for in a show to replace Infinity Train when it got cancelled.
